<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" />{{rh|226|THE GOSPEL|CHA. IIII.}}</noinclude>{{hwe|band.|husband.}} {{sc|Iesvs}} saith to her, Thou hast said vvel, that I haue no husband. {{verse|chapter=4|verse=18}}† For thou hast had fiue husbands: and he vvhom thou novv hast, is not thy husband. this thou hast said truely.

{{verse|chapter=4|verse=19}}† The vvoman saith to him, Lord, I perceiue that thou art a Prophet. {{verse|chapter=4|verse=20}}† {{sup|‖}} Our fathers adored in this mountaine, and you say, {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Deu. 12, 6. Ps. 121. 13.''}}* that at Hierusalem is the place vvhere men must adore. {{verse|chapter=4|verse=21}}† {{sc|Iesvs}} saith to her, VVoman beleeue me, that the houre shal come, vvhen you shal neither in this mountaine, nor in Hierusalem adore the Father. {{verse|chapter=4|verse=22}}† {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''4. Reg. 17, 28. 36.''}}* You adore that you knovv not: vve adore that vve knovv, for saluation is of the Ievves. {{verse|chapter=4|verse=23}}† But the houre commeth, and novv it is, vvhen the true adorers shal adore the Father {{sup|‖}} in spirit and veritie. for the Father also seeketh such, to adore him. {{verse|chapter=4|verse=24}}† God is a spirit, and they that adore him, must adore in spirit and veritie. {{verse|chapter=4|verse=25}}† The vvoman saith to him, I knovv that {{sc|Messias}} commeth, (vvhich is called {{sc|Christ}}): therfore when he commeth, he vvil shevv vs al things. {{verse|chapter=4|verse=26}}† {{sc|Iesvs}} saith to her, I am he, that speake with thee.

{{verse|chapter=4|verse=27}}† And incontinent his Disciples came: and they marueiled that he talked vvith a vvoman. No man for al that said, VVhat seekest thou, or vvhy talkest thou vvith her?

{{verse|chapter=4|verse=28}}† The woman therfore left her vvater-pot: and she vvent into the citie, and saith to those men, {{verse|chapter=4|verse=29}}† Come, and see a man that hath told me al things vvhatsoeuer I haue done. Is not he {{sc|Christ}}? {{verse|chapter=4|verse=30}}† They vvent forth therfore out of the citie, and came to him.

{{verse|chapter=4|verse=31}}† In the meane time the Disciples desired him, saying, Rabbi eate. {{verse|chapter=4|verse=32}}† But he said to them, I haue meate to eate which you knovv not. {{verse|chapter=4|verse=33}}† The Disciples therfore said one to an other, Hath any man brought him for to eate? {{verse|chapter=4|verse=34}}† {{sc|Iesvs}} saith to them, My meate is to doe the vvil of him that sent me, to perfit his vvorke. {{verse|chapter=4|verse=35}}† Doe not you say that yet there are foure moneths, and haruest commeth? Behold I say to you, lift vp your eies, and see the countries, that they are vvhite already to haruest. {{verse|chapter=4|verse=36}}† And he that reapeth, receiueth hire, and gathereth fruite vnto life euerlasting: that both he that sovveth, and he that reapeth, may reioyce together. {{verse|chapter=4|verse=37}}† For in this is the saying true: that it is one man that sovveth, and it is an other that reapeth. {{verse|chapter=4|verse=38}}† I haue sent you to reape that vvhich you laboured not: others haue laboured, and you haue entred into their labours.<noinclude>{{rh|||haue}}</noinclude>
